newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up sharply on housing report.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up sharply on housing report.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended sharply higher on support from a bullish U.S. housing starts report, but profit taking at times and bear spreading kept prices under highs, traders said.
Lumber closed $5.90 to $9.10 higher with January up the least at $390.00 and March up most at $391.70 per tbf.

Traders attributed the bulk of strength to the November U.S. housing starts report. The Commerce Department reported November U.S. housing starts up 9.2 percent to 1.514 million annual rate, the largest rise since an 11.5 percent jump in July 1995.

Futures started higher on demand from the report but ran into profit taking and further bear spreading. January fell for a net loss before renewed commercial buying sparked a rally near mid-morning that took March up the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf. Profit taking then pared prices again late before another round of spreading pushed March back up to near its high, traders said.
The rise in starts exceeded economist estimates and showed the effects of cheaper mortgage rates, according to analysts in the housing industry.
